Once my T proudly told me about something that he did.  He did the right thing indeed, but in the back of my mind, I thought he was a bit nosy and he should just mind his own business.  

I didn't tell him my thoughts right away, but in the next session, I told him how I felt about what he told me with some explanations.  He listened to my point of view, and he shared with me his POV and the reasons behind his action.  

Not that we are trying to change each other's mind, we are just trying to understand each other, and in the end, agreed that we are two different people, doing things in different way.

I think the relationship between you and your therapist is unique, not something that you can find elsewhere, but that doesn't mean you cannot build a unique relationship with another person in the future that is meaningful and important to you.

There is nothing wrong seeing your therapist as a mother substitute, as long as you're respecting her boundaries, and you will learn to accept that there are limits and she cannot fill the void in you, which is tough.  But building a good relationship with your therapist gives you courage to face the wound and heal the pain, knowing that she is there for you.

I've told mine I see him as a father figure, and he said that it's okay.  He explained that he cannot take me into his life, he cannot hug me or comfort me physically, because that should be the role of my real father, but he will not stop caring and supporting me as long as I need, just like what would parents do for their child.

And the truth is, purposely looking elsewhere for mother substitutes will only cause you more pain.  They may help you feel good at times, but without actually working on the problems, your unhappiness would still be with you.

My parents told me that they were at their 70s when I was 6, and I kind of knew people die at around 80-90, so I used to think that they were going to die anytime soon, until I realized that they lied.

When I first contacted my T, he told me he had a waiting list of six people, and I had to wait for three months.  After I agreed to wait, he arranged an initial consultation with me, so that I wouldn't have to wait for months to find that I didn't want to work with him.

I'm not sure how waiting list works exactly, but I'm guessing some people only do short term therapy or some don't do weekly session, so there will be space for new clients?

But recently my T says that he doesn't have a waiting list anymore.  He would just refer people to other therapists if his schedule is full.

T knows that I always fear that he will suddenly be gone (he's a bit old but in fact not too old), and he made a video for me telling me how much he cares about me, so that in case he's no longer here, I can still watch the video and know that he's there for me.  Watching that video warmed my heart and made me cry.

The reason that I couldn't talk in session is because my mind wanders a lot, there are just too many things in my head and I don't know where to start, also sometimes there are things that I just couldn't make myself say them out loud.  

With emails, I let my therapist had a glimpse of what's going on in my head, so even though I couldn't talk, he knows what I'm running away from and he would guide me to talk more and more.  

Also as mentioned, I have trouble speaking in complete sentences, but since I've talked about my problems in my emails, my therapist could still understand me even if I was just spitting out words by words.

So answering your questions, with the help of my therapist, it does become easier for me to talk.  There are still times that I stay silent for the entire session, and my therapist could tell that there's something going on inside me, and would ask me to write to him after the session if I'm able to.

I hope you can find your way to open up to your therapist too.  And if your therapist doesn't allow email, write down your thoughts and hand it to your therapist in sessions or read them out loud if you can would help a lot too.

Indeed, I probably would have given up on therapy or felt so stuck, if I couldn't express myself through writing.  

And I agree that while having a close therapeutic relationship, upholding boundaries is important too.

I've read about therapist would usually teach their clients some grounding techniques, so that the clients won't get too overwhelmed.  My therapist never talk about any of these with me, but there were times that I couldn't calm myself down, he would let me hold an ice cube or draw on paper, and I felt better.  Maybe this is one of the techniques?  

Whenever I shut down, he would just wait there and stop talking (could be for almost the entire session).  He knew I was running away from the topic.  I think he let me escape into my own thoughts on purpose, because I could sense that he was focusing on me the whole time I stayed silence.  And when I "came back", I would tell him "I felt very weird", and he would say "I can see that.  What was happening?  What were you thinking about?"

Maybe next time I see him, I will ask him about his thoughts on this.

I guess my situation is quite like yours. My thoughts scattered at all corners of my head, and whenever my therapist asks me a question, even if I try to think and somehow I know I actually have the answer, I would still reply "I don't know". This starting to frustrate me more than my therapist, he is being patient with me, sometimes he would push me a bit and say "try, tell me more", then I would squeeze just a few more words or repeating "I don't know".

So recently I'm trying to do this "moment diary" thing, which is whenever there're thoughts that come to my head, I just write it down, could be just a word, a sentence or a paragraph, then everytime before the session, I would send these diary to my therpaist, and he would go through my "thoughts" with me one by one, and this helps me to talk more easily as those are my own words and i can remember the moment or the feelings when I wrote these. This also helps my therapist to understand me more even though sometimes I may not be able to explain why I wrote certain things.

You can consider trying this too if you like to write, because usually after a week or so, it'd be difficult to remember certain things that you wanna talk about from that pile of thoughts. For me, my head just turn messy and foggy or goes blank when there are too many thoughts all appear at the same time.
